note:
REBUILT FROM THE CASE-FREE BASE. It had been built before the case was painted off the roof, so idle (empty rack) alternating with idle-break (case present) FLASHED THE LUGGAGE IN AND OUT -- which is what Tyler saw. Nothing failed: two clips of the same object simply disagreed about what it looked like.

The lower leg is measured, not guessed: row profiles find it as a 26px column at x1747-1773 at y680, widening to the hoof by y720. Only the mass BELOW the knee rotates, feathered at the joint so the bend is not a hinge.

0, -4, -9, -12, -9, -4, -1, 0 and then a smaller repeat, because an animal that repeats itself identically is a machine. Negative is backward for a horse facing right.

AN IDLE BREAK, NOT PART OF THE LOOP: the horses breathe constantly and one of them paws every so often. Baked into the loop it would be a tic. Nothing else moves in these frames, and frame 0 is idle frame 0, so it cannot pop.

STORED AT 1.15x THE DRAWN HEIGHT, NOT 2x. R5a's 2x is right for a character; applied to a 956-wide coach across 24 frames it produced 26MB a clip and 70MB across the three, in the REQUIRED boot set because beat 2 stages it -- which is the exact problem R5a was written to prevent. 1.15x is still RESAMPLED at draw time, which was the whole reason 1.00x read wrong, at a third of the pixels.
